question: Crafted using the lost-wax technique in Mohenjo-daro, a significant city of the Indus Valley Civilisation, the prehistoric Dancing Girl figurine is primarily made of which of the following materials?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bronze**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dancing Girl figurine** is one of the most iconic artifacts from the **Indus Valley Civilisation**, which flourished around 2500 BCE.
 
• It was crafted using the **lost-wax technique**, a sophisticated metal casting method. This technique demonstrates the advanced metallurgical skills of the people of the Indus Valley.
 
• The figurine is made of **Bronze**, which was a widely used material during the Indus Valley period for creating tools, ornaments, and art pieces. *Hence, the correct material is *Bronze*.*
 
• It depicts a young girl in a confident pose, with her right hand on her hip and her left hand holding an object. The figurine suggests a remarkable sense of realism and artistry.
 
• The discovery of the Dancing Girl figurine provides evidence of the use of metallurgy and artistic expression in the Indus Valley Civilisation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indus Valley Civilisation:**

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilisation is one of the **world's oldest urban civilisations**, existing between **3300 BCE and 1300 BCE**. Major cities include **Harappa** and **Mohenjo-daro**.
 
• It is known for its advanced urban planning, drainage systems, metallurgy, and craftsmanship.
 
 
 
• **Lost-Wax Technique:**
 
 
• The lost-wax technique involves creating a wax model, covering it with clay or a similar material, and then heating it to melt the wax and create a mold for casting metal objects.
 
• This method was used extensively in ancient civilizations for making intricate metal artifacts and sculptures.
 
 
 
• Bronze **Usage in Ancient Civilizations:**
 
 
• Bronze was a widely used metal during the Bronze Age. It was used for tools, weapons, ornaments, and artistic creations.
 
• The people of the Indus Valley Civilisation were skilled metallurgists and used Bronze extensively for crafting objects like the Dancing Girl figurine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of the Dancing Girl Figurine:**

 
 
• The figurine was discovered in **Mohenjo-daro**, one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation, by archaeologists in **1926**.
 
• It measures approximately **10.5 cm** in height, showcasing the detailed artistry and craftsmanship of the era.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Artifact:**
 
 
• The Dancing Girl figurine provides valuable insights into the social and cultural aspects of the Indus Valley Civilisation, indicating an appreciation for art and aesthetics.
 
• It also highlights the advanced metallurgical capabilities of the civilisation, as Bronze casting requires significant skill.
